svg.title: Two real additions preserve the population standard deviation but produce different means
svg.desc: The original observations two, four, six and eight have count four, total twenty, sum of squares one hundred twenty, mean five and population variance five. Add a real value z. The count becomes five. The new variance is four plus four twenty-fifths times z minus five squared. Setting it equal to the original variance five gives z minus five squared equal to twenty-five quarters. There are two valid branches, z equal to five halves or fifteen halves. The graph shows both filled intersections with the horizontal variance-five line and the minimum at z five, variance four. Adding five halves gives new mean nine halves; adding fifteen halves gives mean eleven halves. Both five-record datasets have population standard deviation square root five. Keep both branches unless an original condition rules one out. The formula allows all real additions although the graph displays a finite window.
